##   A way to take scattering read-plane from LBM4S and make a nice animation.

scatter_animdata = scatter[100:200,...,1,0].cpu().numpy()

from matplotlib import animation
from IPython.display import HTML
fig = plt.figure()
def anim_func(t):
    return plt.imshow(scatter_animdata[t])
ani = animation.FuncAnimation(fig, anim_func, frames=scatter_animdata.shape[0])
#HTML(ani.to_html5_video())
from matplotlib.animation import FFMpegWriter
writer = FFMpegWriter(fps=15, metadata=dict(artist='jawonl'), bitrate=400)
ani.save("surf_backscatter_field_HH.gif", writer=writer)



##   A basic porosity cluster-finding algorithm

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

poro = torch.rand((1,1,30,30,30)) < 0.1
dtype, device = torch.float32, 'cpu'
N,C,Li,Wi,Di = poro.shape
percol = ((torch.rand((1,1,Li,Wi,Di),device=device) < 0.1) * poro).to(torch.float16) # select with 10% chance a gas or brine cell
percol[percol > 0] = torch.arange((percol > 0).sum()).to(torch.float16)

for i in range(20):
    nb = F.max_pool3d(percol, kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=1)
    propo = poro * (nb > 0) * (percol==0) > 0
    percol[propo > 0] = nb[propo]

plt.imshow(percol[0,0,10].detach().cpu().numpy()); plt.title('clusters'); plt.colorbar(); plt.show()
plt.imshow(poro[0,0,10].detach().cpu().numpy()); plt.title('porosity'); plt.colorbar(); plt.show()
